candidates.thesis_hold_conditions: Hold as long as: $523B backlog converting at >$3B/quarter to revenue; OCI cloud growth >30% YoY; Stargate data centers opening on schedule; debt/capex ratio not deteriorating further
candidates.thesis_break_triggers: EXIT if: OpenAI cancels or material renegotiates Stargate contract OR OCI cloud growth falls below 20% for 2+ quarters OR Ellison announces capex expansion without revenue backing OR interest coverage ratio falls below 3x
candidates.key_catalysts: $523B backlog revenue recognition; OCI data center openings (Abilene TX operational, new sites 2026); Stargate expansion to 7GW; Sept earnings.
candidates.key_risks: Capex exceeds OCF by $21.8B YTD — unsustainable without backlog conversion; debt-financed buildout; OpenAI contract renegotiation; data center delivery delays; 16x PE could compress further if growth disappoints.
candidates.analyst_note: ORCL is the most asymmetric setup in our universe today: 78% upside to analyst consensus at $141.60, $523B backlog that dwarfs the current $180B market cap, and the Stargate anchor tenant relationship with OpenAI. The reason it crashed 59% from $346: Ellison is spending $39.2B capex vs $17.4B operating cash flow — the market is pricing balance sheet risk. That risk is real and the position sizing should reflect it (5% max, not 15%). But if the backlog converts at even 50% efficiency, this stock doubles from here. MEDIUM conviction with upside-skewed asymmetry.
